**Observations:**

- W1 rows for border pixels (row 0 except cols 12–15, row 27 cols 0–3 and 24–27, parts of cols 0 and 27, the outer corners) all sit in roughly ±0.036 — exactly the PyTorch default U(−1/√784, 1/√784) initialization range. These pixels evidently never carried signal, so their weights never moved; this is expected behaviour (no weight decay). The trained region is nearly full-frame (rows 1–27, cols 2–25), which fits a Fashion-MNIST-like dataset rather than MNIST digits.
- Inside the trained region every hidden unit's weight map is spatially smooth: neighbouring pixels (left/right and above/below) have similar values for the same unit, and features are blob/stripe-shaped, e.g. unit 0: strong negative patch rows 12–14, cols 21–25 (down to −0.72) with a positive patch rows 9–11, cols 24–26 (+0.4 to +0.52); unit 15: positive band rows 2–3, cols 6–13 (~+0.3 to +0.43) and rows 12–13, cols 22–24 (+0.46 to +0.60); unit 7: positive blob rows 12–17, cols 4–10 (peak ~0.5); unit 4: positive top-center (rows 2–4) and a negative vertical stripe around col 21, rows 22–24 (~−0.44); units 2/3/5/6: positive bottom rows 26–27 center; units 6/10/11: negative top-center. Largest |W1| ≈ 0.72; typical trained magnitudes 0.1–0.4.
- I specifically checked all four corners and all edge strips for isolated large weights (a classic patch/pixel trigger) and found none; every moderately large weight has similarly sized neighbours. The bottom-center row-27 weights (inputs 769–773, up to ±0.35) differ from row 26 but are spread across many units with mixed signs, not concentrated into one unit → one class.
- No dead units (every unit has substantial W1 weights), no duplicated units, no unit with a tiny weight map plus a large W2 row.
- b1 in ±0.41, b2 in ±0.22 — ordinary.
- W2 is dense with nearly all |w| between 0.3 and 0.95 (max |−1.071| at unit 10→class 5), with few near-zero entries and little visible correlation between columns of semantically similar classes. That is somewhat bland-looking, but with only 16 hidden units and heavy sharing it is within what ordinary training can produce; no row or column is an outlier in magnitude or sign pattern.

**Unusual:** no

**What:** nothing

**Confidence:** 30%
